key_insight: This paper explores whether coding agents can automate the creation of generalized task and motion planning (TAMP) solutions, reducing the need for hand-built, TAMP-specific engineering. The main idea is that agents can synthesize reusable planning logic that transfers across problem instances.
problem_solved: Task and motion planning is hard because discrete task choices must satisfy geometric, kinematic, and dynamic constraints at the same time. Even with full observability and object-centric state information, solving new TAMP instances usually requires extensive expert-crafted engineering.
method: Investigate coding agents as a way to synthesize planning components for generalized TAMP.
Leverage regularities across related planning instances to reduce effort on unseen problems.
Evaluate whether agent-generated code can replace or reduce manual TAMP-specific system design.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a path toward more automated planning system development, lowering the barrier to deploying TAMP in new domains. If effective, coding agents could make advanced robotics planning more scalable and less dependent on specialized human expertise.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing coding agent -> synthesized planner -> TAMP solution on new instances

Comparison chart of manual engineering vs agent-generated planning workflow

paper_title: Coding Agents for Generalized Task and Motion Planning Problems
paper_authors: Matteo Merler, Bowen Li, Josh Roy, Yichao Liang, Qianwei Wang
